Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Ethan Kim (Redwood SE); Maya Rodriguez (Thera - Head of ML Ops), Amir Patel (Thera - Platform Engineer), Sophie Turner (Thera - PM)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Welcome to the Thera onboarding kickoff. I'm Jordan, AE on the account, with Priya our CSM and Ethan SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Maya (Thera): Good, thanks. Excited to start, we've been waiting to get things moving.
[00:14] Amir (Thera): Yep, thanks for coordinating. We've got some compliance questions up front so wanted to make sure we cover those.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood CSM): Absolutely, we'll go through security and then deployment options and a proposed timeline. Jordan, do you want to kick off with goals?
[00:28] Jordan: Sure. High level, Thera wants to move from prototype to production inference for two features: clinical summarization and patient triage scoring. The goal for this quarter is a pilot in staging and then a production rollout in Q2. Success criteria Maya mentioned were latency under 300ms for short summaries and cost per inference under $0.02 on average. Is that still right Maya?
[00:45] Maya: That's right, roughly those numbers. For triage scoring we care more about model consistency and auditability.
[00:52] Sophie (Thera PM): Also want to make sure role-based access and audit logs are available for post-launch compliance.
[00:59] Ethan (Redwood SE): Great, makes sense. Quick note on terminology: when we talk caching please note KV cache sometimes gets transcribed odd like \"K V cash\" but that's KV cache which helps latency for repeated contexts.
[01:10] Amir: Nice, yeah we were looking at your docs last night. One question - do you do private deployments? We have some data residency and network requirements.
[01:18] Jordan: Yes, Redwood supports Hosted API for quick start, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) for stricter controls. For Thera we recommend starting in Hosted for speed if acceptable, or Dedicated staging with a VPC peering if you need network isolation.
[01:36] Maya: What's the gap between Dedicated and Private? Is Private fully air-gapped?
[01:40] Priya: Private is the more controlled option - you get a customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem package for air-gapped needs. Dedicated gives isolation at the tenant level with reserved GPUs but still runs in Redwood's managed infra; you can add VPC peering and strict egress rules.
[01:55] Amir: Ok. For now we probably need VPC peering and KMS integration, not full air gap.
[02:00] Jordan: That's common. Ethan, do you want to talk about how we handle KMS and SSO?
[02:04] Ethan: Sure. We integrate with customer KMS/HSM for encryption-at-rest keys and support SSO via SAML/SCIM for provisioning. Our audit logs capture token-level calls, and we can retain logs per your retention policy. There might be an additional compliance add-on if you need extended retention.
[02:21] Sophie: Do you have SOC 2 or ISO docs we can share with our security team?
[02:25] Priya: Yes, we'll send the SOC 2 report and our security whitepaper. Jordan will include the link in the follow-up.
[02:30] Jordan: I'll send SOC2, ISO summary and the full security packet - and also the onboarding runbook link: https://redwood.ai/onboarding/thera-boot (note: placeholder link).
[02:40] Maya: Great. Regarding benchmarks - we want to validate latency and cost. Can you run an initial benchmark with our workload?
[02:47] Ethan: Yep. For the pilot we'll provision a staging tenant and run throughput and p99 latency tests. For the benchmarking we'll need a sample of your typical prompt sizes and token distribution, plus expected concurrency. If you can share 1k example requests and average token length that'd be perfect.
[03:02] Amir: We can export a CSV with 1k requests. We'll also include peak QPS and a 95th percentile expectation.
[03:09] Jordan: Perfect. Tentative plan: Thera provides samples by Friday, Redwood runs a benchmark the following week and we share results. If the numbers look good we spin up a Dedicated staging pool and start a two-week pilot.
[03:22] Maya: Sounds good. On pricing - can you share Dedicated vs Hosted cost examples?
[03:26] Jordan: We'll send a pricing summary. For Hosted you pay per token; for Dedicated you reserve capacity with monthly commits which reduces unit cost for steady workloads. Our Optimize toolkit will recommend batching/quantization profiles to reduce cost.
[03:39] Sophie: Do you support quantized models? We want to squeeze costs without losing quality.
[03:42] Ethan: Yes, we support quantization profiles and model recommendations. We'll run quality checks tied to your eval prompts - Evaluate on the same prompt set to ensure no regression.
[03:50] Amir: Any competitors to be aware of for the deployment model? We asked about Anthropic and using hosted APIs from other providers.
[03:56] Jordan: Customers look at Anthropic, OpenAI, and managed cloud endpoints like SageMaker. Difference for Redwood is a unified runtime across modes and tooling for cost control - plus rollout and fallback policies for reliability.
[04:08] Maya: Good. On timelines - what are realistic dates? You said pilot next week if we share data by Friday.
[04:14] Priya: We'll aim for a staging benchmark the week of 2026-03-09 and a dedicated staging pool by 2026-03-16. That puts production rollout planning into late March/early April depending on results.
[04:24] Sophie: Ok that fits our Q2 roadmap.
[04:27] Jordan: Quick question for the engineers - Amir, are you able to accept VPC peering or do you prefer Private deployment?
[04:33] Amir: VPC peering with KMS integration is preferred. Full private/on-prem is heavier for now.
[04:38] Ethan: Great - for VPC peering we'll need a CIDR range and a contact for peering setup. I'll include an infra checklist in the follow-up.
[04:46] Amir: I'll send the CIDR and a contact.
[04:49] Maya: Also need to confirm data retention and deletion API support.
[04:53] Priya: We have deletion APIs and configurable retention. We'll include those endpoints in the runbook.
[04:58] Jordan: Alright, let's capture next steps. Priya, do you want to read them?
[05:02] Priya: Sure. Action items: Jordan to send onboarding runbook, SOC2, and pricing. Priya to set up weekly cadence and project plan. Ethan to run initial benchmark in staging once Thera provides sample payloads. Thera to share 1k request examples, CIDR for VPC peering, and success criteria.
[05:20] Maya: Good. One more question - for model versioning and rollouts can we pin a version and have canary rollouts?
[05:26] Ethan: Yes, Redwood supports pinning model versions and rollouts including canary and automatic fallback policies. We can show that in the next technical deep dive.
[05:34] Sophie: Great. Anything else?
[05:36] Jordan: Nothing major. We'll follow up with a doc bundle and calendar invites. Thanks everyone for your time.
[05:42] Maya: Thanks, talk soon.
[05:44] Amir: Thanks.
[05:45] End of meeting.
